newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares mixed as buyers bide time-traders.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares mixed as buyers bide time-traders.

text.p: Russian shares ended mixed on Thursday in lacklustre trading as Western investors waited for better buys in a market still in the doldrums, traders said.

"Prices are at a level that most investors think represent value, but the investors are leery of entering a market that could well go down another 10 percent and present better buying opportunities later," said Troika-Dialog's Terry Olin.
"There is a vacuum where there should be orders."
Mosenergo closed at $0.9300, down from Wednesday's close of $0.9375 on the Russian Trading System (RTS).
LUKoil rose to $8.97 from $8.79, and Norilsk Nickel ticked down to $6.75 from $6.78.
The RTS Index edged down 0.40 percent to $166.06 on $12.1 million reported volume.
But Olin said strong buying in a leading stock could turn the market.
Renaissance Capital head trader Anton Kudryashov said market news was mixed for the day, leaving stocks little changed.
Central Bank chairman Sergei Dubinin said late on Wednesday that Russia spent $1.6 billion to support the rouble in August.

Kudryashov said the market, which took the news poorly, thought such support could be tied to the International Monetary Fund's lack of an announcement that it will disburse the next tranche of its $10.2 billion loan to Moscow this month.

But he said President Boris Yeltsin's plan to transfer power to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin during heart surgery, which the president said would be at the end of the month, had diffused fears of a prolonged Kremlin power struggle.
One trader said a rumour that Norilsk Nickel would issue new stock to pay debts may have sent fears of dilution into the market and accounted for a slight edging down in the metals group's shares.
